headline: Bears Hold the Floor as Energy Outpaces a Broadly Retreating Market
body_html:
Monday's midday session is shaping up as a defensive slog, with decliners outpacing advancers by more than two to one — 372 names lower against just 174 in positive territory across our 549-name universe. The dominant theme is geopolitical: tensions surrounding Iran's Kharg Island oil infrastructure have sent crude higher, lifting Energy to the top of the sector leaderboard with a gain of roughly 0.46%, the lone bright spot in an otherwise retreating tape. Homebuilders, Consumer, and Materials are bearing the brunt of the selling, down 1.22%, 1.18%, and 0.91%, respectively.

Tesla is the session's standout mover, surging nearly 5% to lead all gainers. Roblox and e.l.f. Beauty are each up better than 4%, joined by CrowdStrike — which is bucking the broader tech malaise on what appears to be sector-rotation interest into cybersecurity names. On the other side of the ledger, TransMedics Group and Burlington Stores are both off roughly 6%, while Clorox and Shopify are each shedding close to 4%.

Into the close, traders will be watching crude's trajectory and any fresh headlines out of the Middle East. A sustained oil bid could keep Energy afloat, but the weight of selling across Consumer and Industrials suggests month-end portfolio rebalancing may amplify volatility in the final hour.

briefs.headline: Kharg Island Risk Keeps Oil Market on Edge
briefs.body: Crude prices have climbed as concern mounts over potential disruptions to Iran's Kharg Island export terminal amid an ongoing regional conflict. Analysts cited by wire services suggest oil could hold above the $80-per-barrel threshold as Middle East supply risks persist, providing a tailwind for Energy equities mid-session.

briefs.headline: Tesla Charges to the Head of the Pack
briefs.body: Tesla is up nearly 5% and stands as the session's top percentage gainer, pulling ahead of the field without an obvious single catalyst beyond continued momentum interest. The move is helping Auto-Tech punch well above its weight on an otherwise difficult tape dominated by broad-based selling.

briefs.headline: Burlington and TransMedics Lead the Decliners Board
briefs.body: Burlington Stores and TransMedics Group are each shedding close to 6%, making them the hardest-hit names in the universe through midday. Burlington's drop adds pressure to an already weak off-price retail picture, while TransMedics' slide weighs on the already-struggling Healthcare-Devices corner of the market.

briefs.headline: CrowdStrike Defies the Tape in Cybersecurity
briefs.body: CrowdStrike is advancing more than 4% Monday, standing out as one of the few technology names in positive territory. The move appears tied to rotation into security-focused software at a time when broader tech and software sectors are flat to modestly negative, according to market observers.

briefs.headline: Europe Posts Fifth Straight Monthly Gain Despite Monday Dip
briefs.body: The STOXX 600 slipped in Monday's European session as rising oil prices weighed on sentiment, yet the index still secured its fifth consecutive monthly advance — a streak that underscores resilient demand for European equities even as geopolitical crosscurrents intensify across the region and Middle East.

briefs.headline: Turkey Advances Grain Corridor Talks and Domestic EV Stake
briefs.body: Ankara said it has a plan for Black Sea grain shipments and remains in active dialogue with both Russia and Ukraine, a development that could ease agricultural commodity pressure. Separately, Turkey's sovereign wealth fund is set to take a stake in domestic electric-vehicle maker TOGG as existing industrial shareholders exit the register.
